research_question: In preterm infants (<37 weeks' gestation) at risk of bronchopulmonary dysplasia, does early (initiated before 7 days of postnatal age), low cumulative dose (<2 mg/kg) systemic dexamethasone, compared with placebo or no treatment, reduce the combined outcome of death or BPD (oxygen requirement) at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age?
treatment_label: Early low-dose systemic dexamethasone (<2 mg/kg cumulative, started <7 days of age)
outcome_description: Number of infants who died or had bronchopulmonary dysplasia (oxygen requirement / chronic lung disease / oxygen dependence) at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age, out of the number randomised to each arm (intention-to-treat denominator). Deaths before 36 weeks are added to survivors with BPD when reported separately.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g (equivalently RR < 1) means fewer infants died or developed BPD at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age in the early low-dose dexamethasone group than in the placebo/no-treatment group — i.e. the result favours dexamethasone.
search_queries: early dexamethasone preterm infants randomised trial bronchopulmonary dysplasia
low dose dexamethasone chronic lung disease prematurity placebo controlled trial
postnatal corticosteroids first week of life ventilated preterm neonates death or BPD 36 weeks
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in infants born before 37 weeks' gestation
Compares systemic dexamethasone begun in the first week of life (before 7 days of postnatal age) with placebo or no treatment
Reports quantitative data allowing calculation of death and/or BPD/chronic lung disease/oxygen dependence at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age (events and numbers randomised)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, narrative review, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between a dexamethasone treatment arm and a placebo/no-treatment control arm (e.g. control is hydrocortisone, another steroid, or a different dexamethasone dose only)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts/proportions, means+SDs, t/F values, or odds/risk ratios)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. inhaled or intratracheal steroids, hydrocortisone trials, dexamethasone started at 7 days or later, cumulative dexamethasone dose 2 mg/kg or more, or dexamethasone given solely to facilitate extubation in infants ventilator-dependent after 7 days)
moderators_to_extract: Age at initiation of treatment (hours/days of life)
Mean gestational age or birth weight of the trial population
Risk of bias (blinding, allocation concealment) and sample size category
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio using a fixed-effect Mantel-Haenszel model where available, otherwise random effects. Events = infants dead or with BPD (oxygen requirement) at 36 weeks' PMA; total = number randomised to each arm. For multi-arm trials use only the low-dose dexamethasone arm (<2 mg/kg cumulative, started <7 days) and the placebo/no-treatment arm, combining arms that fall within the same dose category and ignoring other steroid arms.
single_outcome_target: Death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age
